sentences.text: At anchor, the signals are given at intervals of not more than one minute.
A vessel at anchor rings the bell rapidly for about five seconds.
A vessel one hundred meters or more rings the bell in the fore part, then immediately sounds the gong rapidly for about five seconds in the after part.
A vessel at anchor may also sound one short, one prolonged and one short blast to warn an approaching vessel.
A vessel engaged in fishing at anchor, or a restricted vessel working at anchor, sounds one prolonged and two short instead of the anchor signals.
A vessel aground gives the bell signal, plus the gong if required, with three separate and distinct strokes on the bell immediately before and after the rapid ringing.
